What One Builder and His AI Assistant Shipped

Jason Nutt · Front-end developer, support & solutions engineer, founder of TruVINE — the production record behind this portfolio.

Panel 1

The Cold Open

From a simple Bible reader to a production studio

“It started as a simple Bible reader…” It didn’t stay simple. Working solo, after hours, I — together with Judah, my AI assistant — built it into a complete production operation: a 78-book Bible app with a complete audio Bible, an animated film studio run on a locked character system, a YouTube channel with an automation layer, and a merch store. This page is the record: what shipped, how it was made, and the standard it was held to.

The Voice

Panel 3

The Cast

Character packages — designed once, locked

Seventeen character builds in the Mark package: Jesus, the Twelve, Mary His mother, Mary Magdalene, John the Baptist, Pilate. The rule: a character is designed once, locked, and stays the same face in every film, forever. Each book gets a complete character package on this template — sheets, trading cards, portraits, group shots — so a multi-film series never drifts.

Panel 4

The Family Package

The same system, applied to real people

For my son Jude’s birthday film, the cast was my own family — built as locked characters under the same system. These are the actual canonical portraits the film is generated from:

How “locked” works — every character carries a written locks list: for Jason, buzz-cut hair thin on top with grey at the temples · purple glasses · short beard, grey at the chin · a slim nose with a subtle once-broken bend · a dark tribal tattoo on the upper left arm and nowhere else. Measurements are in the file too — Jude stands about an inch taller than his dad now, and Gavin is the shortest of the three. Once a lock is written, nobody improvises: not the director, not the assistant, not the generator. Britney’s portrait took twelve documented versions to land — versioned, reviewed, approved. Likeness, treated as QA.
Panel 5

The Director’s Gate

The QA discipline I authored — how a scene earns its place
1

The Director’s Pass

Every scene is reviewed against the story it has to tell — notes taken in plain language.

2

The Evidence

Suspected defects are proven, not debated — frame-by-frame sampling, waveform and loudness analysis.

3

The Verdict

Confirmed or not, in writing, with the evidence frames attached. The written record is the spec.

4

The Remake

Failures are banked with retake briefs and rebuilt from the package. Nothing ships that hasn’t passed.

“Characters from the package lead, and the scene follows them — not the other way around.”

The Package Leads — studio law, codified in the production standard

Case study. A review cut shipped an identity morph — hidden behind the lead character, invisible to still-frame checks. Review caught it by eye; dense frame sampling proved it; the verdict was written with evidence frames; and the segment was scrapped and rebuilt fresh from the family package. The lesson became a gate: identity continuity is audited in motion, including through occlusions — on every scene, in every production since.
